title: Your $300,000 in XLY Holds $125,585 in Amazon and Tesla Alone
detail:

Quick Read

Amazon and Tesla control 42% of XLY, turning a fund that sounds like broad consumer spending into a bet on two stocks.

Amazon rose 16% and Tesla fell 13% this year, leaving XLY nearly flat at just 1%.

Anyone holding a broad market index fund likely owns Amazon and Tesla twice, so total exposure across every account deserves a check.

Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

Picture a retiree with a hypothetical $300,000 in the State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (NYSEARCA:XLY). The name suggests a piece of everyday American spending: stores, restaurants, hotels, and cars, but the fund's SEC portfolio holdings filing tells a narrower story. As of June 30, 2026, two companies, Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA), made up 41.86% of net assets. On that hypothetical portfolio, $125,585 sits in just two stocks.

Sean Gallup / Staff / Getty Images Europe
Two Stocks Claim Over $125,000 of a Hypothetical $300,000

Here is the split. Amazon carried a 22.22% weight, or $66,665 of the hypothetical position. Tesla carried 19.64%, or $58,921. Both weights come from the filing dated June 30, 2026, when net assets totaled roughly $22.59 billion.

The fund listed 51 positions in that filing. The drop after the top two is steep. Home Depot held 5.83%, McDonald's 4.15%, TJX 3.92%, and Booking Holdings 3.44%. Each of those household brands carried a fraction of either leader's weight, while cruise lines, auto parts retailers, and homebuilders also appear in the filing, mostly at small weights. Holders who think they own "consumer spending" also own a concentrated position in two companies.

How a Sector Fund Ends Up This Lopsided

XLY seeks to track the Consumer Discretionary Select Sector Index. That index aims to represent the consumer discretionary sector of the S&P 500, according to the fund's fact sheet. Sector indexes that weight holdings by company size give the most room to the biggest companies, and when a sector contains a few giants, those giants can dominate the basket.

title: Tech Leaders Want Jensen Huang to Return to Nvidia. Here’s What That Would Mean for the Stock Price.
detail:
Tech Leaders Want Jensen Huang to Return to Nvidia. Here’s What That Would Mean for the Stock Price.
Adria Cimino, The Motley Fool
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 5:35 PM CST 5 min read
NVDA
SPCX
TSLA
SHOP
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Jensen Huang shocked the market last week when he stepped down from his position as chief executive officer at one of the world's most famous companies, Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA). His move followed allegations of affairs that arose just days earlier. Though some investors predicted a possible resignation, it still seemed somewhat surprising, as Huang founded the company more than 30 years ago and led its spectacular success story.

Today, however, some tech leaders and general Huang supporters aren't ready to say goodbye to Huang. In fact, they are fighting for him to come back. A petition for that purpose has drawn more than 176,000 signatures, including more than 92,000 shareholders and several big names in technology, such as Space Exploration Technologies and Tesla chief Elon Musk, and Shopify CEO Tobias Lütke.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Let's consider if a Jensen Huang return really could happen -- and find out what such an event could mean for the stock price.

Jensen Huang. Image source: Nvidia.

Allegations and an investigation

First, a quick note about Nvidia's recent turmoil. Huang stepped down last week following allegations of an affair with a person U.S. intelligence calls a Chinese spy and allegations of a separate affair with an Nvidia executive. Nvidia's board opened an investigation into the former, but remained supportive of Huang. The company then met to discuss the company's future after reports of the second alleged affair emerged -- and Huang's resignation followed.

Nvidia named chief financial officer, Colette Kress, to take on the role of CEO on an interim basis while a search is conducted for a permanent replacement.

CEOs are always key to a company, but Nvidia's Huang had taken that importance to a new level. Sporting a leather jacket and speaking about AI in a comfortable, engaging manner, Huang reached superstar status -- and followed through on this by guiding the company along the path of explosive growth.

Huang's decisions helped Nvidia become the world's AI chip leader and maintain the position even as competition intensified. A visionary, Huang always seemed a step ahead and wisely broadened Nvidia's presence across the AI movement through partnerships and acquisitions -- the latest being the decision to buy open-source AI platform Hugging Face. Huang also maintained solid relationships with tech leaders across the AI spectrum.

title: Tesla's Cybertruck exit reveals an expensive gamble
detail:
Tesla's Cybertruck exit reveals an expensive gamble
Faizan Farooque
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 3:33 PM CST 5 min read
TSLA
Trade Tesla on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Tesla's Cybertruck was supposed to change America's pickup market.

Rather, only four years after deliveries started, the electric vehicle is nearing the end of its manufacturing cycle.

Tesla (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk plans to discontinue the Cybertruck in 2027, freeing manufacturing capacity at the company's Texas factory for its Cybercab robotaxi.

The choice represents a withdrawal from one of Tesla's most ambitious car launches.

The greater surprise, however, is what Musk is prepared to give up.

Although the Cybertruck hasn't been able to draw in customers, Tesla is preparing to replace its manufacturing capacity with a driverless car whose long-term economic potential remains uncertain.

Tesla's Cybertruck is near the end

Musk originally planned to halt manufacturing in the middle of 2027, but to complete more unfulfilled orders, he decided to prolong production to the end of summer 2027.

Additionally, he has cautioned that many customers who may not get their trucks would need to have their deposits returned by Tesla.

The company plans to redirect manufacturing resources toward the Cybercab, which has become central to Musk's autonomous-driving ambitions, according to Reuters.

Beyond the fate of a single electric pickup, the decision poses questions for investors.

Is it possible for Tesla to generate more money creating robotaxis than selling cars to regular Americans?

Related: Tesla and Nvidia just found another AI bottleneck

Tesla's Cybertruck fell far short of Musk's expectations

Musk said that the Cybertruck, which Tesla announced in 2019, might rival the most well-liked pickup trucks in America.

In the past, he proposed that Tesla could sell 250,000 units annually.

The real world turned out to be quite different.

U.S. Cybertruck sales declined 48% to just 20,237 vehicles in 2025, according to Reuters.

That amount is only about 8% of Musk's previous yearly sales goal.

Pricing was another issue with the Cybertruck.

The $39,900 starting price was replaced by much more expensive models when deliveries began in late 2023.

More Tesla:

Tesla wants to sell a car with no steering wheel this year

Its divisive stainless-steel design, recalls, and restricted international market prospects made the truck's challenges worse.

Meanwhile, the more reasonably priced Model 3 and Model Y remained crucial to Tesla's overall business.

The Cybertruck was intended to increase Tesla's market share in the lucrative pickup industry in the United States. Rather, it served as a warning that technical innovation does not always result in demand from the general public.

Partnership kicks off with a November 19 webinar and brings Silvia's users education on income strategies beyond traditional fixed income

NEW YORK, Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Direxion, a leading provider of specialized ETFs with approximately $70.8 billion in assets under management (as of September 30, 2026), today announced a partnership with Silvia, Inc. (Nasdaq: SVIA), the first publicly traded agentic finance firm.

Direxion

Through the partnership, Direxion will provide Silvia's users with webinars, content and other resources on pursuing income beyond traditional fixed income strategies, including options-based approaches such as Direxion's Defined Income Boost ETFs, which seek to generate income from stocks many investors already follow: NVIDIA, Tesla, Alphabet, Meta, Palantir and Micron.

"Investors make better decisions when they are well informed, especially on something as important as generating income. We're pleased to partner with Anthony, who clearly shares our passion for education, as illustrated by his mission to build the Silvia platform, which is designed to help investors feel more confident and prepared as they plan for the income they need," said Douglas Yones, Chief Executive Officer at Direxion.

The partnership will launch with an inaugural webinar for Silvia's users on Thursday, November 19, at 2 p.m. ET, featuring a conversation between Anthony Pompliano, Chairman and CEO of Silvia, Inc., and Bilal Little, Global ETF Strategist at Direxion. The partnership will continue into 2027 with additional collaborations in the works.

Silvia was co-founded by Anthony Pompliano, an entrepreneur, investor and best-selling author. "Our mission is to help independent investors make money," said Mr. Pompliano. "Partnering with Direxion on educational content gives our users access to clear, practical information about strategies they may want to evaluate as part of their broader financial picture."

Direxion is best known for its leadership in leveraged and inverse ETFs, particularly in technology, with funds such as the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull & Bear 3X Shares (SOXL/SOXS), among the most actively traded ETFs globally*, the Direxion Daily TSLA Bull 2X and Bear 1X Shares (TSLL/TSLS), and the Direxion Daily SpaceX Bull & Bear 2X ETFs (LOFF/LOFD). The firm recently announced plans to launch the Direxion Daily Anthropic Bull & Bear 2X ETFs (ANTO/ANTD), expected to begin trading on the first trading day after Anthropic's IPO.

*Bloomberg, as of October 31, 2026, based on average daily trading volume / dollar volume among globally listed ETFs.

title: Tesla's Cybercab Comes With a Monthly Catch
detail:
Tesla's Cybercab Comes With a Monthly Catch
Moz Farooque ACCA
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 1:35 PM CST 2 min read
TSLA
Trade Tesla on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) is inviting select customers to buy its Cybercab for personal use, taking the driverless two-seater beyond its company-operated Robotaxi fleet.

The car starts at $29,990, with a required $299 monthly subscription that buyers need to keep it running.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 7 Warning Signs with TSLA.

Is TSLA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

TSLA GF Value chart

The Cybercab has no steering wheel or pedals, so owners have no manual driving option if they cancel the subscription. The vehicle can operate only in areas Tesla's Robotaxi service covers, which include parts of several cities in Texas and Florida. Tesla estimates that deliveries will begin in December, Business Insider reported.

The initial purchase terms also bar owners from using their Cybercabs commercially. That means early buyers can't put their vehicles on Tesla's Robotaxi network to earn fares, an option CEO Elon Musk previously pitched as part of the company's autonomous ride-hailing plans.

Musk said on X that the Cybercab would become available nationwide as Tesla secures regulatory approvals. He also called the $299 monthly fee too high and said it should be closer to the roughly $115 Tesla charges for Full Self-Driving and connectivity on other models, Reuters reported.

Investors Takeaway

The December delivery window is the first test of whether Tesla can move from taking orders to putting privately owned Cybercabs on the road. Beyond that, the price and the service map will shape how many people can use one. At the announced rate, the subscription adds $3,588 a year. A lower fee could make ownership more appealing while reducing recurring revenue per vehicle. A broader rollout would show whether Tesla can attract buyers who want the Cybercab for everyday trips without the ability to earn fares.

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Release Date: November 16, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript.

Positive Points

OmniOne revenue increased 105% year-over-year to $1.1 million, driven by the launch of OmniOne for Quest with Meta.

Total revenue grew 21% year-over-year and 55% sequentially to $1.2 million.

OmniOne unit orders increased 230% year-over-year, and enterprise orders rose 45%, including follow-on orders from Tesla and NASA.

The proposed acquisition of STS International could accelerate defense strategy by providing established contract vehicles, security clearances, and past performance, with STS reporting approximately $40 million in unaudited cash-basis revenue for the 10 months ended October 31, 2026.

The company identified approximately $600,000 in avoidable expenses, averaging about $200,000 per month, as part of its path to profitability.

Negative Points

Gross margin declined to 25% from 41% year-over-year, reflecting a shift from higher-margin legacy Omni Arena sales to OmniOne.

Net loss widened to $6.4 million from $1.9 million in the prior year period, and adjusted EBITDA loss increased to $3.6 million from $1.2 million.

Cash and cash equivalents decreased to $5 million from $9.5 million at fiscal year-end, with cash used in operations of $3.6 million in the quarter.

The STS International acquisition is subject to a non-binding letter of intent, and its financials are unaudited, cash-basis, and may differ materially; no definitive financing commitment has been obtained for the $8 million cash consideration.

Operating expenses rose significantly to $5.1 million from $1.9 million, driven by public company costs and increased marketing spend.

Q & A Highlights

Q: With the STS International acquisition pending, what are the long-term revenue mix and gross margin implications if it closes? A: CEO Jan Goetgeluk said it is too early to disclose detailed revenue mix or margin implications. However, he noted STS reported approximately $40 million in unaudited cash-basis revenue for the 10 months ended October 31, 2026, which would be meaningful relative to Virtuix's current revenue base if the deal closes, subject to audit and change.

Q: If the STS acquisition does not close, what are the capital raising plans given the need to reduce burn rate? A: CEO Jan Goetgeluk said Virtuix is laser-focused on its path to profitability through five key drivers: scaling consumer revenue, growing high-margin enterprise sales, advancing defense programs, completing the STS acquisition, and reducing costs. He added that the company believes it has access to financing options to bridge to profitability, but the near-term focus is reducing burn through higher revenue and lower corporate overhead, accounting, and investor relations costs.
